tagline: A leading global media and entertainment company that creates and distributes a differentiated and comprehensive portfolio of content and products across television, film, streaming, interactive gaming, publishing, themed experiences, and consumer products
hero_kpi_rationale: The Streaming segment is the primary driver of growth and strategic transformation for WBD, with HBO Max at the center of business model revitalization in response to linear decline.

kpis.name: Streaming Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Number of subscribers to HBO Max and other streaming services within the group.
kpis.description: Streaming subscriber base increased 13% in 2025, driven by HBO Max international expansion, growing from 116.9 million in 2024 to 131.6 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in streaming subscribers driven by global expansion of HBO Max despite challenging sector environment.

kpis.name: Distribution Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenues from fees paid by distributors (cable, satellite, streaming).
kpis.description: Distribution revenue declined 2% in 2025, impacted by domestic linear subscriber loss (9%), partially offset by increased domestic affiliate rates (3%) and streaming subscriber growth (13%).
kpis.signal: Partial stabilization despite decline in linear subscribers, offset by increased affiliate rates and streaming growth.

kpis.name: Advertising Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenues generated from selling advertising inventory on linear and digital platforms.
kpis.description: Advertising revenue declined 11% in 2025, primarily driven by 25% collapse in domestic linear network audiences, partially offset by increased HBO Max ad-lite subscribers.
kpis.signal: Sharp advertising revenue decline driven by 25% collapse in domestic linear network audiences, partially offset by…

kpis.name: Content Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenues from production and licensing of films, series, games, and sports rights.
kpis.description: Content revenue declined 7% in 2025, affected by unfavorable comparison with $576 million in Olympic rights sublicensing revenue in Europe in 2024, as well as lower gaming revenues.
kpis.signal: Revenue decline reflects unfavorable comparison with non-recurring Olympic rights sublicensing in 2024 and lower…

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Operating profit after costs, but before interest and taxes.
kpis.description: Shift from $10.032 billion operating loss in 2024 to $738 million operating profit in 2025, driven by reduced depreciation and restructuring charges.
kpis.signal: Return to operating profitability after massive losses driven by reduced depreciation and amortization charges.

kpis.name: Depreciation and Amortization
kpis.explanation: Charge related to amortization of intangible assets, notably content rights.
kpis.description: Declined 19% in 2025, down from $7.037 billion in 2024, related to reduced amortization of content rights following prior asset impairments.
kpis.signal: Marked reduction in depreciation and amortization reflecting lower asset base following prior period impairments.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA margin following accelerated deleveraging.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin following accelerated deleveraging.

kpis.name: Net Debt
kpis.explanation: Massive $16 billion deleveraging over 4 years, key prior to NFLX deal.
kpis.description: Massive $16 billion deleveraging over 4 years, key prior to NFLX deal.

kpis.name: Studios Revenue
kpis.explanation: Barbie/Wonka box office behind, 2026 slate equals Superman.
kpis.description: Barbie/Wonka box office behind, 2026 slate equals Superman.

kpis.name: Streaming Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Number of subscribers to HBO Max and other streaming services within the group.
kpis.description: Streaming subscriber base increased 13% in 2025, driven by HBO Max international expansion, growing from 116.9 million to 131.6 million subscribers.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in streaming subscribers driven by global expansion of HBO Max despite challenging sector environment.

kpis.name: Domestic Linear Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Number of subscribers to linear channels in the United States.
kpis.description: Declined 9% in 2025, reflecting structural shift toward streaming, with domestic linear subscribers decreasing from 65.2 million in 2024 to 59.2 million in 2025.
kpis.signal: Continued cord-cutting trend reflecting structural shift from traditional television to streaming platforms.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks including attacks on its systems and data. While cybersecurity is important, language in the filing is standard for media companies with digital platforms.

risks.title: Litigation
risks.score_rationale: The company is involved in legal proceedings, but no specific material litigation mentioned in the filing demonstrates elevated risk beyond typical industry exposure.

risks.title: Regulation
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to standard regulations common to media and entertainment companies operating globally, including data protection and cybersecurity requirements.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in an intensely competitive environment across streaming, linear television, and film production, with significant competitive pressures from major tech and entertainment competitors.

risks.title: Multiemployer Pension Plans
risks.score_rationale: The company participates in multiemployer defined benefit pension plans, which could subject it to liabilities if plans become underfunded or if the company withdraws participation.

risks.title: Linear Television Decline
risks.score_rationale: Structural decline in linear television viewership (25% audience decline in domestic networks in 2025) and subscribers (9% decline) represents a fundamental shift in consumer behavior away from traditional television.

risks.title: Geopolitics
risks.score_rationale: The company operates globally and is exposed to geopolitical risks, but no specific material geopolitical issues are highlighted in the filing.

risks.title: Technology
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to technology risks including streaming platform reliability and digital content distribution, but these are managed through standard operational practices.

ai_positioning.summary: WBD does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
